subject: Human Body
title: Colon Sections and Transit
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Colon Sections and Transit.

hook.text: Waste travels up the right side, across the top, and down the left side of your abdomen. It's a U-shaped route.

buildup.text: Four sections: ascending, transverse, descending, and sigmoid colon. Each curves into the next.

discovery.text: Transit through the colon takes 12–36 hours. Slow waves called haustral contractions move contents along gently.

twist.text: Fiber speeds transit. Without it, waste stagnates, hardens, and leads to constipation and straining.

climax.text: The colon moves slowly by design. More time in the colon means more water recovered and firmer stool.

punchline.text: Slow transit is a feature, not a flaw.

quiz.question: Why does transit through the colon take 12–36 hours?
options: Slow movement allows maximum water absorption
Muscles in the colon are weak
